correctness.rationale: For all integers n>=4, p,q in (0,1), two protected vertices disconnect a simple cycle into two paths. The escape probability at i is (1-q)(A+B r^(i-1))(A+B r^(s-i)), giving H_s=cs-K+f(s) and additive E_n. A strict infection-set coupling makes zero-length arcs nonoptimal. Exact f differences change sign at theta; f(m)<0 and f(s)->0 force any globally optimal short arc to remain bounded, and the eventually increasing tail breaks the integer-theta tie for m=floor(theta)+1. An elementary difference comparison proves all finite n at p=q=1/2. Exact-independent-bond enumeration (385 cases), finite differences and large-n examples all passed; the proof, not enumeration, handles infinity.

value.rationale: Exact optimization of two node-protection choices in the cycle is a natural finite network intervention problem. An explicit expectation and all-parameter limiting optimizer discover a stable finite gap even as graph size increases; the rare-seeding asymptotics and p=q=1/2 exact phase exception give useful interpretable boundaries. This is more than checking a preset finite configuration or rediscovering that targeted vaccination can help.
